subject.title: [Bug]: Scheduled isolated agentTurn outer run records error although session ended success

question: Should OpenClaw fix this narrow cron bug by preserving execution `status=ok` with delivery failure fields, or should this wait for a first-class warning/partial-success status?
rationale: Both paths solve the misleading success/error boundary, but they expose different public cron status semantics and affect status-only operators, backoff, and alerting.

options.title: Accept Narrow Status Split
options.body: Land the direct fix candidate so successful isolated execution remains `ok` and delivery failures are surfaced through delivery-specific fields.

options.title: Defer To Warning Status
options.body: Keep this issue open under the broader warning-status work if maintainers want a new partial-success cron status across CLI, UI, protocol, and plugin surfaces.

options.title: Require Live Scheduled Repro First
options.body: Pause the fix until a real scheduled Gateway/provider run reproduces and validates the exact WSL2/Feishu path.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Status Split
recommendation.body: Land the direct fix candidate so successful isolated execution remains `ok` and delivery failures are surfaced through delivery-specific fields.

likelyOwner.reason: The delivery-dispatch boundary and public cron semantics trace back to Peter Steinberger’s feature-history work, making him the best routing candidate for the status-contract decision.
